{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-8","id":"msg_011CeCZzgzZrL9ik84JRnoFr","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_012R8eTXdH2UVot3MoHhJJDd","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/ssd/workspace/buidlguidl/ethskills-evals-test/artifacts/frontend-playbook-quiz-004/2026-08-19T181859Z-claude-with-skill-2/workspace/answer.md","content":"# Why the static export breaks on Node 25 (`localStorage.getItem is not a function`)\n\n## TL;DR\n\n- **What changed:** Recent Node added the Web Storage API. `globalThis.localStorage`\n  is no longer guaranteed to be `undefined` on the server. It is now a *global that\n  exists but is not the browser's `localStorage`*.\n- **Teammate A is wrong** because the premise \"Node has no localStorage\" describes\n  Node ≤ 21. It's out of date.\n- **Teammate B's fix can't work** because the prerender does not run in the process\n  where `instrumentation.ts` installs the polyfill, and because the problem is a\n  *present* `localStorage`, not a *missing* one. Adding another one solves nothing.\n- **The fix:** stop using the presence of `localStorage` to detect the browser, and\n  keep browser-only storage access out of prerender. Detect `window`, not\n  `localStorage`.\n\n---\n\n## 1. What actually changed in Node\n\nNode.js gained a built-in **Web Storage API** (`localStorage` / `sessionStorage` as\nglobals). It landed experimentally in Node 22.4 behind `--experimental-webstorage`\nand has been moving toward on-by-default. By the time CI jumped to Node 25, the\nbuild runtime is exposing these globals (either because the flag is now default, or\nbecause something in the toolchain/`NODE_OPTIONS` turns it on).\n\nThe important part is not that Node \"has localStorage now.\" It's *what kind* of\nobject it is:\n\n```\n# Node with Web Storage enabled but no backing file (the build's situation):\ntypeof localStorage        -> defined (not \"undefined\")\nlocalStorage               -> a runtime accessor that is NOT a usable Storage\nlocalStorage.getItem(...)  -> blows up\n```\n\nI verified this against the installed Node:\n\n- **Without** Web Storage enabled: `typeof localStorage === 'undefined'` — the old world.\n- **With** `--experimental-webstorage` but no valid `--localstorage-file`: touching\n  `localStorage` fails (`ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE` for the empty location) — it is\n  *present in the global scope but not a working `Storage`*.\n- **With** a valid `--localstorage-file`: `getItem` exists and round-trips.\n\nSo on the CI box, `localStorage` has flipped from \"not there\" to \"there but not a\nreal browser Storage.\" That single change is the whole bug.\n\n## 2. Why Teammate A's mental model is out of date\n\nA's reasoning — *\"Node has no localStorage, so there is nothing to call `getItem` on,\ntherefore the error is impossible\"* — was correct through **Node 21**. It is false on\nNode 22.4+ and on Node 25.\n\nThe Scaffold-ETH 2 stack (wagmi / RainbowKit / SE2 hooks and helpers) historically\nuses the **absence** of `localStorage` as its \"am I on the server?\" signal, e.g.:\n\n```ts\nconst storage = typeof localStorage !== \"undefined\" ? localStorage : noopStorage;\nstorage.getItem(\"...\");  // runs on the server now\n```\n\nWhile `localStorage` was `undefined` in Node, this guard correctly picked the\nserver-safe branch. Now the guard sees a defined-but-broken global, takes the\n\"browser\" branch **during prerender**, and calls `getItem` on something that isn't a\nreal Storage. That is exactly the crash on `/_not-found`. The error isn't\nimpossible — it is the *direct consequence* of the guard A assumed could never fail.\n\n## 3. Why Teammate B's polyfill can't fix it — where the prerender runs\n\nB's fix has two independent fatal problems.\n\n### (a) The prerender runs in a different process from `instrumentation.ts`\n\n`instrumentation.ts`'s `register()` hook runs once when a **Next.js server instance**\nboots. Static export is not that. During `next build`, Next.js prerenders each route\nin **separate short-lived worker processes** (the static-generation / render workers\nit spawns via `jest-worker`/child processes). The worker that renders\n`/_not-found` is not the process that ran `register()`, and the instrumentation hook\nis not guaranteed to execute in those export workers at all.\n\nSo no matter how correct the polyfill is, it is installed in the *wrong* runtime.\nThe process that actually touches `localStorage.getItem` never sees it. The build\nfails **identically** — which is exactly what B observed.\n\n### (b) The bug is a *present* localStorage, not a *missing* one\n\nA polyfill is the answer when a global is **absent** and code needs it. Here the\nglobal is **present** (that's the whole problem) and browser-only code should simply\nnot run on the server. Adding another `localStorage`:\n\n- doesn't stop the browser branch of the guard from executing during prerender, and\n- can't reliably override Node's built-in global anyway — it's exposed as a runtime\n  accessor on `globalThis`; reassigning it from user code loads too late (Node has\n  already installed its own) and may be ignored.\n\nYou cannot polyfill your way out of \"the wrong code path is running.\" You have to\nstop it from running.\n\n## 4. What actually fixes it\n\nThe root cause is **environment detection by the wrong signal.** Fix that, and keep\nstorage access out of prerender.\n\n1. **Detect the server with `window`, not `localStorage`.** `window` is still\n   `undefined` in Node; `localStorage` no longer is. Anywhere in your code (or a\n   thin shim over a dependency) that does `typeof localStorage !== \"undefined\"` to\n   mean \"in the browser,\" change it to:\n\n   ```ts\n   const isBrowser = typeof window !== \"undefined\";\n   ```\n\n2. **Keep browser-only storage access out of prerender.** Read `localStorage` inside\n   `useEffect` (which never runs during prerender), or render the offending component\n   client-only:\n\n   ```ts\n   const Wallet = dynamic(() => import(\"./Wallet\"), { ssr: false });\n   ```\n\n3. **Give wagmi an SSR-safe storage.** Modern wagmi already guards on `window`:\n\n   ```ts\n   import { createStorage, noopStorage, cookieStorage } from \"wagmi\";\n\n   createStorage({\n     storage: typeof window !== \"undefined\" ? window.localStorage : noopStorage,\n     // or cookieStorage for SSR-persisted state\n   });\n   ```\n\n   Make sure your wagmi/RainbowKit/SE2 versions are current enough that they don't\n   reach for `localStorage` at module-eval time on the server.\n\n4. **Immediate unblock (stopgap, not the fix):** ensure the build runtime is *not*\n   enabling Web Storage — check `NODE_OPTIONS` for `--experimental-webstorage` and\n   drop it, so `localStorage` returns to `undefined` and the existing guards work\n   again. Do this only to get CI green while you land fixes 1–3; it stops working the\n   day Web Storage becomes default-on, which is the direction Node is heading.\n\n### The one-line takeaway\n\nThe old guards feature-detected the **environment** by probing a global that used to\nbe browser-exclusive. Node made that global universal. Detect the **capability you\nactually need** (`window`, or \"did this run in an effect on the client?\"), not a\nglobal that Node has since adopted — and the export stops depending on `localStorage`\nbeing absent.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1178,"cache_read_input_tokens":18434,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1178},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"cc2968df-f188-4633-998f-8a3a44603eb3","uuid":"32cc195f-9909-472c-82fd-dcd89a381293","timestamp":"2026-08-19T18:21:36.048Z","request_id":"req_011CeCZzg9xmGtkpRHNGYMjW"}

The short version:\n\n**What changed in Node.** Recent Node ships the Web Storage API — `localStorage`/`sessionStorage` as globals (experimental in Node 22.4, moving to default-on). By Node 25 the build runtime exposes them. I verified locally: with Web Storage off, `typeof localStorage === 'undefined'`; with it on but no backing file, touching `localStorage` *fails* — it's present in global scope but is **not a usable browser `Storage`**.\n\n**Why A is wrong.** \"Node has no localStorage\" was true through Node 21. The SE2 stack (wagmi/RainbowKit) historically detects the server via `typeof localStorage === 'undefined'`. Now that global is defined-but-broken, so the guard takes the *browser* branch during prerender and calls `getItem` on a non-Storage → the exact crash. The error isn't impossible; it's the direct result of the guard A assumes can't fail.\n\n**Why B's polyfill can't work.** Two independent reasons:\n1. **Where the prerender runs.** `next build` prerenders each route in *separate worker processes* it spawns, not the server instance where `instrumentation.ts`'s `register()` runs. The worker rendering `/_not-found` never executes the polyfill — so the build fails identically.\n2. **Wrong shape of fix.** The problem is a *present* `localStorage`, not a missing one. Polyfilling adds another one; it doesn't stop browser-only code from running server-side, and you can't reliably override Node's built-in global from user code anyway.\n\n**What fixes it.** Detect the browser with `typeof window !== 'undefined'` (window is still undefined in Node; localStorage isn't), keep storage access in `useEffect` or `dynamic(..., { ssr: false })`, give wagmi an SSR-safe storage (`noopStorage`/`cookieStorage`), and update the stack. Immediate stopgap: drop `--experimental-webstorage` from `NODE_OPTIONS` so the old guards work — but that's temporary, since Node is heading toward default-on."}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":5860,"cache_read_input_tokens":19612,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":5860},"output_tokens":2,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"cc2968df-f188-4633-998f-8a3a44603eb3","uuid":"de420a33-c18d-4a89-a653-10d1dd771fc9","timestamp":"2026-08-19T18:21:46.348Z","request_id":"req_011CeCa6zVhESTDMoin7Ypkm"}
